security_audit.summary: Most Markdown backtick detections are false positives for filenames, component names, skill names, or fenced formatting. Confirmed risks are actual p11 CLI execution, unpinned global npm installation, and publishing through bearer edit URLs. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed skill files.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before npm global install or npx execution. Prefer a trusted existing CLI, or pin and verify the package version.
Validate p11 IDs, URLs, versions, and local paths before command execution. Pass arguments without shell interpolation and reject suspicious targets.

remediation.issue: Publishing changes through bearer edit URLs
remediation.suggestion: Show the planned changes and ask for confirmation before running p11 share. Treat edit URLs as secrets and return them only when needed.

remediation.issue: Edit URLs may appear in chat transcripts
remediation.suggestion: Return read URLs by default. Share edit URLs only after the user asks, and remind users not to place them in public channels.

content.user_title: Revise p11 Documents From Review Comments
content.value_statement: Reviewer comments can be hard to turn into a clean published revision. This skill finds the p11 target, applies clear decisions, and shares a new version.
actual_capabilities: Resolve a p11 target from a read URL, edit URL, document ID, source file, chat context, or p11 history.
Fetch visible reviewer comments and replies with the p11 CLI before editing.
Classify review threads as clear decisions or items that need clarification.
Apply clear reviewer decisions to a static p11 TSX document.
Check the document against supported p11 component and interaction rules.
Publish a revised version through the existing p11 edit URL.
limitations: It depends on a trusted p11 CLI installation and valid p11 authentication.
It should not decide ambiguous or conflicting reviewer threads without user guidance.
It is limited to p11 document components and static document content.
Publishing requires careful handling of edit URLs because they grant document write access.

use_cases.title: Apply review decisions before a stakeholder update
use_cases.description: Turn approved comments into a revised p11 document and publish the new version for reviewers.

use_cases.title: Prepare a clean product review artifact
use_cases.description: Resolve comments on a proposal or launch plan while keeping unresolved questions separate.

use_cases.title: Maintain technical design documents
use_cases.description: Update a p11 technical document from reviewer feedback while preserving supported document components.

prompt_templates.title: Revise the latest document
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: use the most recent p11 document already discussed in the chat.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use p11:revise on the latest p11 document from this chat. Apply clear reviewer comments and ask me about unclear threads.

prompt_templates.title: Revise a specific target
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: provide the target so the skill does not need history lookup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use p11:revise for this p11 read or edit URL: [paste URL]. Apply clear comments and summarize any skipped threads.

prompt_templates.title: Handle clarification first
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: separate clear decisions from questions before publishing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use p11:revise for [document target]. If a thread is unclear, draft clarification replies and wait before publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Revise with publish approval
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review planned changes before the final p11 share step.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use p11:revise for [document target] from version [number]. Show the planned changes first, then publish only after I approve.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks to shorten the introduction and replace one term across the document.
output_examples.output: The response lists the applied edits, notes that all visible threads were clear, and provides the updated read link.

output_examples.input: One thread asks for a wording change, and another thread contains disagreement between reviewers.
output_examples.output: The response applies the wording change, asks whether to clarify or skip the disputed thread, and waits before publishing.

output_examples.input: A user gives an edit URL and asks to publish a revised proposal after comments are resolved.
output_examples.output: The response confirms the target, summarizes resolved comments, publishes the new revision, and handles the edit link carefully.

best_practices: Provide the p11 read or edit URL and the source TSX file when possible.
Resolve unclear reviewer threads before asking the skill to publish a revision.
Review the planned changes and protect edit URLs as document write credentials.
anti_patterns: Running the skill without a target when the latest p11 history item may be unrelated.
Publishing while reviewer comments still contain disagreement or open questions.
Posting p11 edit URLs in public channels or long-lived shared transcripts.

faq.question: Does this skill create new p11 documents?
faq.answer: No. It revises an existing p11 document and publishes a new version through an edit URL.

faq.question: Can it handle unresolved reviewer comments?
faq.answer: It can identify them, but it should ask for clarification or skip them only with user approval.

faq.question: Does it need the p11 CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses the p11 CLI to read comments, access docs, and publish revisions.

faq.question: Will it edit interactive app components?
faq.answer: No. The skill is designed for static p11 documents that use supported document components.

faq.question: Why are edit URLs sensitive?
faq.answer: An edit URL can grant write access to a p11 document. Treat it like a credential.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude Code, Claude, and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Claude Code, and Codex workflows.
